gallery.filename: Beirut Peacekeeping Chapel Sign after explosion.jpg
gallery.title: File:Beirut Peacekeeping Chapel Sign after explosion.jpg
gallery.credit: Archivisit, U.S. Naval Chaplaincy School, Armed Forces Chaplaincy Center
gallery.source: Beirut Peacekeeping Chapel Sign after explosion
gallery.description:
The sign for the Peacekeeping Chapel, Beirut, Lebanon, during the time that U.S. forces were part of the International Peacekeeping Force.  On October 23, 1983, when a suicide bomber drove a truck laden with explosions into the Marine Barracks, this portion of the sign survived. It is part of the historical collection at the U.S. Naval Chaplaincy School and Center, on the campus of the Armed Forces Chaplaincy Center (AFCC), Ft. Jackson, Columbia, SC.  
In the article, "With the Marines in Beirut," published in the Fall 1984 issue of "The Jewish Spectator," Rabbi Arnold Resnicoff, one of the Navy chaplains present during the attack, wrote:  "Amidst the rubble, we found the plywood board which we had made for our "Peace-keeping Chapel."  The Chaplain Corps Seal had been hand-painted, with the words "Peace-keeping" above it, and "Chapel" beneath.  Now "Peace-keeping" was legible, but the bottom of the plaque was destroyed, with only a few burned and splintered pieces of wood remaining.  The idea of peace - above; the reality of war - below."[1]

Official photo from the U.S. Naval Chaplaincy School and Center.
categories: Military chapels of the United States

gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: From left to right, U.S. Marine Corps Cpl. Gerrett Ogle, Lance Cpl. Stephen Carrera, and U.S. Navy Petty Officer 2nd Class Armando Tejeda, with 8th Marine Regiment, 2d Marine Division serve as wreath bearers during the 30th Beirut Memorial observation ceremony in Jacksonville, N.C., Oct. 23, 2013. The ceremony was held to remember the service members that died in the Oct. 23, 1983 bombing of 1st Battalion, 8th Marines Headquarters building in Beirut, Lebanon. (DoD photo by Lance Cpl. Cesar N. Contreras Camera, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:Beirut Salute (10461909976).jpg
gallery.artist: Marines from Arlington, VA, United States
gallery.description:
Marines with 8th Marine Regiment march fire a 21-gun salute during a Beirut Memorial Observance Ceremony at the Lejeune Memorial Gardens in Jacksonville, N.C., Oct. 23. The observance marked the 30th anniversary of the deadly Marine barracks bombing in Beirut, Lebanon.

(U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Charles Clark/Released)
